Bull Markets vs Bear Markets

Illustration for bull markets vs bear markets.

Bull and bear market describe sustained rises and declines over a defined market and period. Twenty-percent changes are common conventions, not universal definitions or instructions. An individual share, a price index and a total-return index can tell different stories.

💡
Example

An invented index rising from 100 to 120 gains 20%. Falling from 120 to 96 then loses 20%, leaving it 4% below the original 100. A percentage decline and equal percentage recovery do not cancel each other.

State the starting point and whether dividends are included.
A regime label often becomes clear retrospectively; it does not identify the next turning point.
Buying a dip can precede a further decline. Moving to cash can miss a recovery. Neither action follows automatically from the label.
Pro Tip

Compare continuation and reversal scenarios from the same starting observation. Avoid selecting only a period in which every dip later recovered.

Identifying Trend Reversals

A trend reversal is a change in a chosen historical trend definition. In real time, the next observations are unknown. Moving-average crosses, divergences and chart shapes can produce false or late descriptions; none is a reliable turning-point detector by itself.

💡
Example

Hypothetical closes rise 100, 102, 104, then fall 103, 101, 99. A three-close average moves from 102 to 103 to about 102.67 to 101. The average turns after the price peak, illustrating lag rather than an advance warning.

Define the trend rule, interval and lookback before evaluating it.
Record cases where an apparent turn resumed the prior direction.
Distinguish a price-indicator divergence from proof of future momentum; settings change the comparison.
Pro Tip

A retrospective annotation is useful for describing a chart. To evaluate predictive value would require a defined method, unseen data and realistic costs; this exercise does not establish that value.

Volume Analysis

Volume counts traded units during a specified interval and coverage. Every executed transaction has a buyer and a seller, so a large bar alone does not reveal which side has superior information or whether institutions are accumulating.

💡
Example

If the chosen historical average is 1,000 units and the current comparable interval trades 3,000, volume is three times that average. That arithmetic does not establish a continuation probability. A subsequent price can rise, fall or remain flat.

Keep intervals comparable: a partial session and a complete session can be misleading to compare.
State whether volume covers one venue or a consolidated feed, and check for missing data.
A price breakout with higher volume records price and activity observations; it does not confirm a real breakout or guarantee follow-through.
Pro Tip

TradeHQ may display cached provider observations or generated chart data. A generated volume bar is a practice illustration, not evidence of actual market orders or participant intent.

Market Sentiment Indicators
Volatility is not direction

The Cboe VIX Index derives an annualized, approximately 30-day expected volatility measure from S&P 500 index option prices. It is not a forecast that shares will rise or fall, and expected volatility can differ from realized volatility. Fixed VIX thresholds do not identify a guaranteed market top or bottom.

Specify the put/call ratio basis
💡
Example

An invented interval with 600 put contracts and 400 call contracts traded has a volume put/call ratio of 600 ÷ 400 = 1.5. An open-interest ratio uses outstanding contracts instead and can be different. Specify market coverage, date and basis before comparing ratios.

Puts and calls can be bought or written, used for hedges or combined with other positions. A headline ratio does not reveal net directional intent or establish a contrarian trade. Survey responses and social posts also represent selected populations, not every investor.

Pro Tip

Record what an indicator measures and what it cannot establish. Compare two possible later price paths under the same indicator observation instead of treating fear or optimism as a timing rule.
